pages.lesson:
LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASSES: ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When is it necessary to describe a noun?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text
2. use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences
3. value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASSES: ADJECTIVES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1 WORD CLASSES: ADJECTIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives to a partner. (skill: use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text.
3. Practise this skill: use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences.
4. Practise this skill: value the need for correct use of adjectives in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When is it necessary to describe a noun?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 5.3.1 Word Classes: adjectives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify gradable and non-gradable adjectives from a text.
5. Be able to: use gradable and the non- gradable adjectives in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
